outcome: No result found that narrows the gap between the known lower bound (0.082n) and upper bound (n/6 + o(n)) on the maximum pathwidth of n-vertex cubic graphs since 26 January 2024; the Fomin–Høie (2005/2006) bounds remain the state of the art.
summary: The problem asks for the largest possible pathwidth of an n-vertex cubic (3-regular) graph, expressed as a fraction of n. As of January 2024 the known bounds, both due to Fomin and Høie ('Pathwidth of cubic graphs and exact algorithms', Information Processing Letters, 2005/2006), are: pathwidth ≤ n/6 + o(n) for all sufficiently large cubic graphs, and there exist cubic graphs with pathwidth ≥ 0.082n, leaving an open gap between ~0.082n and ~0.167n. I searched broadly for any 2024–2026 work that narrows this specific gap — general pathwidth-of-cubic-graphs bounds, treewidth-of-cubic-graphs results, and adjacent pathwidth literature (path partitions in subcubic graphs, polynomial pathwidth bounds for graphs edge-coverable by k shortest paths, pathwidth-η deletion kernelization, spectral treewidth lower bounds) — and found nothing that addresses the cubic-graph pathwidth extremal question itself. The current Wikipedia 'Pathwidth' article (fetched live) still states the bounds in exactly the 2006 form, with no updates. Related but out-of-scope 2024–2026 papers exist (e.g. on treewidth-of-cubic-graphs NP-completeness, and pathwidth bounds for other graph classes), but none change what a careful reader would write in this bullet. This agrees with the triage pass's 'none' verdict; I do not disagree with it.
competing_reading: None of the adjacent papers found (e.g. 'A polynomial bound on the pathwidth of graphs edge-coverable by k shortest paths', arXiv 2510.02901, or treewidth-of-cubic-graphs NP-completeness work) bear on the extremal question asked here; they concern different graph classes or different parameters (treewidth vs. pathwidth, or different structural restrictions), so none is a plausible case of this problem under a looser reading.
what_would_settle_it: A paper that either exhibits cubic graphs with pathwidth exceeding 0.082n (improving the lower bound) or proves a pathwidth upper bound below n/6 for cubic graphs (improving Fomin–Høie's upper bound), for arbitrarily large n.
